---
title: "Benchmark framework"
---

## Responsibilities

| Layer | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `sblr` | Statistical models, samplers and public inference APIs |
| `sblrbench` | Simulations, strict alignment, oracle checks, adapters, truth-aware metrics, provenance and reference benchmarks |
| Study repositories | Frozen publication-specific designs, production settings, figures, tables and manuscripts |

## Study flow

```text
data preparation
→ simulation
→ oracle validation
→ method fitting
→ standardized extraction
→ metrics
→ credible-set evaluation
→ reproducible report
```

Prediction studies replace credible-set evaluation with held-out prediction and paired model/representation contrasts. Their allele frequencies, genotype scaling, sparse LD, and summary statistics are learned from training individuals only. Test phenotypes are used only by evaluation metrics.

`targets` orchestrates and caches computational studies. Published reports never trigger those analyses: they consume reviewed, frozen compact outputs from a versioned reference capsule.

## Adding a benchmark

1. Promote reviewed compact results into a new versioned directory under `results/reference/`.
2. Add one report using the standard section order.
3. Add one catalogue entry to `studies/index.qmd`.
4. Render the site.

Every study separates a readable **worked example**, a fast **developer smoke test**, the complete targets-based benchmark, and a reviewed compact **reference capsule**. A separate future study may compare single-trait and multi-trait prediction after computational performance has been assessed. Parameter-estimation and convergence studies are planned separately and can reuse retained native fits without changing prediction metrics.
